title: Table Service Standards
blurb: The simple, consistent standards of serving, clearing and checking back that make guests feel properly looked after.
siteNotes: Whether the venue's house style differs from the general serving and clearing rule
Tray and plate-carrying standards used at the venue
legalNotes: CHECK: serve from the left, clear and pour from the right is traditional service etiquette, stated in the trainer as a general rule rather than a legal requirement; confirm it matches the venue's house style.

cards.title: Table Service Standards
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- serve and clear smoothly and safely
- use the check back to catch problems early
- be attentive without hovering

cards.title: Consistency is the key word
cards.body: Polished table service is something guests notice without quite knowing why. It is built from simple standards that any of us can deliver once we know them: the same high standard at every table, every shift.

cards.title: The etiquette
cards.body:
As a general rule, serve food from the guest's left, and clear from the right. Pour drinks from the right. The golden rule is to do it smoothly and without reaching across a guest.

> Never overload yourself. A dropped tray is dramatic and dangerous.

cards.title: Small habit, big impact
cards.body: A minute or two after the food lands, return to make sure everything is right: "How's everything tasting?" It catches a problem while it is still easily fixable, and shows guests you care.

cards.title: Read the table
cards.body: Keep the table tidy throughout, clearing finished plates, empties and crumbs so it never feels neglected. Anticipate what is needed and be there at the right moment without breathing down their necks.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Same high standard at every table, every shift
- Serve from the left, clear and pour from the right, without reaching across
- Never overload a tray
- Check back a minute or two after the food lands
- Be attentive without hovering

cards.q: Consistency means the same high standard at every table, every shift.
cards.why: Consistency is the key word in table service.

cards.q: As a general rule, you clear plates from the guest's…
options: Whichever side is nearest
Left
Right
Front
cards.why: Serve from the left and clear from the right, without reaching across a guest.

options: Returning shortly after serving to make sure all is right
Counting plates against the order at the pass
Checking the bill before it goes to the table
Asking a guest to confirm their order again
cards.why: A check back is a visit a minute or two after the food lands to make sure everything is right.

cards.q: You should overload trays to save trips.
cards.why: Never overload yourself. A dropped tray is dramatic and dangerous.

cards.q: Service should be attentive but not…
options: Friendly
Prompt
Warm
Hovering
cards.why: Be there at the right moment without breathing down their necks.

cards.q: Keeping the table tidy (clearing plates, empties, crumbs) is part of good service.
cards.why: A tidy table never feels neglected.

cards.q: Which of these should a good server anticipate before being asked?
options: Which table the guests would like to move to
A refill, another round or the bill
The guests' dietary needs and allergies
Whether the guests will book again
cards.why: Read the table and anticipate what is needed: a refill, another round, the bill.

cards.q: A dropped tray is both dramatic and dangerous.
cards.why: This is why you should carry plates and trays safely and never overload yourself.

cards.q: The check back helps because it…
options: Reminds guests that they can order more drinks
Adds a little to the final bill for the table
Catches a problem while it is easily fixable
Fills a quiet moment while the kitchen catches up
cards.why: It catches a problem while it is still easily fixable, and shows guests you care.

cards.q: The golden rule is to serve and clear smoothly, without reaching across a guest.
cards.why: Doing it smoothly matters more than any single side rule.
